MEASURED: at 512-wide matrices the polar iteration is a fraction of a percent of a ~297ms step, so the mediator has no throughput arm to trade against and the axis reduces to pure orthogonalization fidelity, which the run shows is already saturated at 5.
name: ns_iteration_budget_v2_measured

activation_observable: secmom_ortho_ratio, which must fall far below 1 to show the buffer left orthogonalized scale, AND secmom_clamp_frac, which must stay near 0 to show it did not fall off the bottom instead. Either alone is insufficient: the ratio rule passed on all three non-engaged runs.
competing_explanation: an effective learning-rate change. Renormalizing the momentum before orthogonalization alters the norm of the matrix fed to the polar iteration, and the iteration's output scale is set by that input; so a win could be nothing but a global step-size change that the same wave would reproduce by moving lr alone. This must be ruled out with an LR-matched arm or by showing the post-NS RMS is preserved. NEW OPPOSING EVIDENCE, registered after the run: a transfer-4 claim from a paper measured at 124M-class scale and exactly 524288 tokens/step reports row-wise second-moment normalization working BETTER after Newton-Schulz than before, which is the baseline's ordering. This mechanism is now a contested bet rather than a favoured one, and a null from the corrected implementation should be read as corroborating that claim.
falsifier: val_bpb of the reordered variant is within the measured within-wave band of its yoked control WHILE the activation observable shows the preconditioner is materially non-identity (pre-NS entrywise rescale ratio far from 1). That combination says the intervention engaged and did nothing. If instead the observable shows the rescale ratio sitting at ~1, the run is INCONCLUSIVE about the mechanism, not evidence against it.
measured_outcome: NOT REFUTED -- NOT ENGAGED. Three runs (precond_pre_slot0, precond_pre_slot1, precond_pre_R1P_C) reported secmom_clamp_frac 0.99789, 0.99791 and 0.99791 against 0.00000 in every yoked control, so 99.8% of the second-moment buffer sat at the clamp_min(1e-10) floor and the arm ran as plain Muon minus NorMuon. The val_bpb deltas (+0.001288, -0.000433, +0.000809) are therefore INCONCLUSIVE about this mechanism. See L014_precond_clamped_out_did_not_engage.
mediator: the entrywise scale distribution of the momentum matrix AT THE MOMENT it enters Newton-Schulz. Orthogonalization is scale-equivariant in a way that discards entrywise second-moment information: normalizing the momentum by its running second moment BEFORE the polar iteration changes which singular directions the iteration is asked to equalize, whereas the same normalization applied AFTER only rescales an already-orthogonalized update and cannot change its direction. IMPLEMENTATION CORRECTED: the momentum is now rescaled to unit RMS per matrix before the second moment is taken, which puts the buffer back in the range its floor and zero-init were designed for. The rescale is a per-matrix scalar and the polar iteration opens by dividing by the Frobenius norm, so it cannot smuggle in an effective learning-rate change.
name: precond_before_ortho_v2_rms_normalized

activation_observable: mean Frobenius norm of the Muon-owned stacked matrices at the final step, printed as muon_weight_norm_final, together with the fraction of entries the cautious mask actually decayed, printed as wd_mask_frac -- the second number is what distinguishes a nominal coefficient change from a delivered one.
competing_explanation: weight decay never reaches equilibrium in this budget. A registered claim puts the equilibrium timescale at order 1000 steps for typical eta/lambda, so at ~1000 steps any effect may be an implicit warmup-shape change rather than the steady-state regularization the source papers measured, and the two are not distinguishable from the final loss alone.
falsifier: moving the decay coefficient across the range the literature disputes leaves val_bpb inside the band in a yoked pair, while the observable confirms the mean weight norm of the hidden matrices actually moved. Note one registered claim holds that Muon without weight decay converges FASTER initially, so this mechanism predicts a sign that may invert at our very short horizon; a null here is genuinely informative. The upward direction has now fired. The remaining live question is DOWNWARD -- wd_const=0.0 -- which one registered claim predicts helps at short horizons and another predicts hurts; that disagreement is unresolved and is the experiment worth a slot.
measured_outcome: REFUTED IN THE UPWARD DIRECTION. wd_const=0.4 against the baseline's 0.2*(1-progress) schedule cost +0.010441 on the 96-107/108-119 pair and +0.008200 on the 120-131/132-143 pair -- both roughly 50x the counterbalanced resolution and roughly 20x the slot offset, so the sign is unambiguous without counterbalancing. Evidence: wd040_slot0, ctrl_R1W_A_slot1, wd040_slot1, ctrl_R1W_B_slot0. Note the arm confounded two factors, a higher mean coefficient AND decay left alive through the warmdown that the baseline switches off; the measurement rules out the pair, not either alone.
mediator: the weight norm of the Muon-owned 2D matrices over the run. The baseline applies a CAUTIOUS decay, masked to entries where update and parameter agree in sign, so the decay actually delivered to those matrices is strictly less than the nominal coefficient and its effective strength is data-dependent rather than set by the schedule.
name: decay_reaches_muon_matrices_v2_measured

activation_observable: muon_param_frac -- Muon-owned parameters divided by all 2D parameters in transformer.h, printed by EVERY arm (control reads 1.000000). Companion observables, both required because the ratio alone cannot distinguish a reassignment from a de-facto learning-rate change: muon_upd_rms_med, the median per-entry RMS of the update applied to the matrices Muon still owns, and adamw_hidden_upd_rms_med, the same statistic for the matrices just demoted to AdamW. The demotion is only an assignment test if the second is within a factor of two of what Muon was delivering to those tensors in the control.
competing_explanation: A LEARNING-RATE FIT, not an assignment effect. The source paper re-tuned per-group learning rates separately in every assignment regime, so its 0.045-nat gap bundles assignment with LR search; and our demoted matrices have no tuned AdamW learning rate at all -- they inherit whatever we pick. A registered claim (o2_muon_hybrid_beats_adamw_at_shared_untuned_lr) says an untuned shared LR favours the Muon hybrid, so an untuned demotion is expected to lose for reasons that have nothing to do with assignment. Discriminating observation: choose the demoted groups' AdamW LR by RMS matching to the Muon update those exact tensors received in the control (MATRIX_LR * shape_factor / sqrt(max(m,n))), and put muon_upd_rms_med and adamw_hidden_upd_rms_med on the record so the match is checkable rather than asserted.
falsifier: ENGAGED-AND-WRONG: muon_param_frac drops from 1.0 to ~0.42, the demoted matrices are demonstrably being stepped by AdamW at an update RMS within a factor of two of the Muon update they replaced (muon_upd_rms_med and adamw_hidden_upd_rms_med bracket each other), and val_bpb is inside the counterbalanced resolution of the yoked control or worse. That says the assignment carries no information at this operating point and the whole restricted-assignment direction is dead here. DID-NOT-ENGAGE: muon_param_frac still reads 1.0, or the demoted groups' update RMS is off by an order of magnitude, which makes the arm an untuned-learning-rate experiment rather than an assignment experiment -- inconclusive, rerun with the RMS matched.
mediator: WHICH of a block's 2D matrices receive a spectral (orthogonalized) update rather than a coordinate-wise adaptive one. Muon's polar iteration equalizes the singular spectrum of whatever matrix it is handed; that is the right conditioning for a matrix whose job is to READ a d_model-dimensional residual stream and write back into it (attn.c_proj, mlp.c_proj), and the wrong one for matrices whose rows serve functionally heterogeneous roles or whose fan-in/fan-out are strongly unbalanced (c_q/c_k/c_v feeding 4 separate heads, mlp.c_fc feeding a squared-ReLU nonlinearity). Our stack hands Muon ALL transformer.h 2D parameters, i.e. 100% of 25.17M matrix parameters; the mediator is the fraction and identity of that set.
name: muon_assignment_by_projection_role

activation_observable: logz_sq_final -- mean of (logsumexp over vocab)^2 averaged over the LAST 10% of training steps, emitted by EVERY arm including the control. The last-10% window is essential: a whole-run average is dominated by the log(8192)=9.0 transient at initialisation (log^2 Z = 81) and would read high even in an arm where the regularizer worked perfectly, which is exactly the ratio-with-no-floor-companion failure L014 was written about. Companion: zloss_frac_of_total (lambda * logz^2 / total loss), which separates 'the term is present and material' from 'lambda was too small to matter' -- the registered null at lambda=1e-4 is precisely the second case.
competing_explanation: AN EFFECTIVE LOGIT-SCALE OR LEARNING-RATE CHANGE ON THE UNEMBEDDING. Penalising log^2 Z applies a large, nearly uniform downward gradient to every logit, which shrinks the lm_head and is equivalent to lowering the effective logit temperature; the model already carries a 15*tanh(z/15) softcap that does the same job by a different route, so a win could be pure logit-scale tuning. Discriminating observations: (1) the existing `softcap` knob is a same-cost arm that changes logit scale WITHOUT constraining log Z -- if moving softcap reproduces the gain, the mechanism is logit scale and not partition regularisation; (2) logz_sq_final must fall by an order of magnitude while zloss_frac_of_total ends small, i.e. the term did its work and then got out of the way, rather than the loss being reduced by trading CE for a shrinking penalty term.
falsifier: ENGAGED-AND-INERT: logz_sq_final is driven below 1.0 while the yoked control's sits an order of magnitude higher, and val_bpb is inside the counterbalanced resolution. That means pinning the partition function buys nothing at 1010 steps, which is the reading two registered claims already predict (the measured benefit of these regularizers was learning-rate headroom, not a lower optimal loss, and at a low base LR all logit interventions were a wash). DID-NOT-ENGAGE: zloss_frac_of_total is under 0.01, i.e. the term never became a material part of the objective -- inconclusive. ENGAGED-AND-DESTRUCTIVE, which is a different verdict from inert: logz_sq_final near 0 with val_bpb worse than the control by more than 0.005 reproduces the catastrophic-lambda regime one size down and bounds the usable band from above.
mediator: the magnitude of the logit partition function log Z = logsumexp(logits) in steady state. Cross-entropy is exactly invariant to a uniform shift of the logits, so nothing in the baseline objective constrains log Z at all: the uniform component of the unembedding is a free direction that the optimizer wanders along. Adding lambda * (log Z)^2 makes that direction the only one the extra term acts on, pinning log Z near 0 and removing a degree of freedom that otherwise consumes unembedding capacity and lm_head gradient variance -- the lm_head is the highest-gradient-variance tensor in the model.
name: zloss_pins_logit_partition

activation_observable: muon_param_frac -- sum of p.numel() over param_groups with kind=='muon' divided by sum over all groups, read off optimizer.param_groups in the epilogue AFTER the charged clock stops (one Python loop, zero FLOPs, nothing near muon_step_fused). CONTROL PRINTS 0.500005; ENGAGED means the treatment prints 0.208331 (+/- 1e-4). Print muon_group_count alongside it (control 4 shape groups, treatment 2) so a config that changed the LR but not the assignment is distinguishable. muon_param_frac is a ratio, so per L014 it carries a companion FLOOR observable: moved_disp_ratio = ||W_final - W_init||_F / ||W_init||_F for the concatenated q/k/v (512,512) tensors and the (2048,512) c_fc tensors, from one clone at step 0 differenced at the end and emitted by BOTH arms. The degeneracy this catches is that the moved matrices land on an AdamW group whose LR is far too small for them and effectively FREEZE: that arm has removed capacity, not changed optimizer scope, and its val_bpb bears on the wrong question. ENGAGED therefore requires moved_disp_ratio within a factor of 2 of the control's value for the SAME tensors; below 0.5x the control it is a non-activation.
competing_explanation: AN EFFECTIVE LEARNING-RATE CHANGE. Moving 14,680,576 parameters from MATRIX_LR=0.04 with spectral normalization onto an AdamW group at some chosen LR means any result is equally consistent with 'MATRIX_LR 0.04 was mis-set on the fan-in-facing matrices', which b3_base_lr_dominates_schedule_shape says should dominate structural stories. TWO DISCRIMINATORS, both required. (1) LR-MATCHED ARM: keep Muon on everything and scale the (512,512) and (2048,512) group LRs by the ratio (treatment moved_disp_ratio / control moved_disp_ratio); if that flat arm reproduces the treatment's val_bpb, the mediator is step size and the mechanism is refuted. (2) MIRROR ARM, which is the one that attributes the effect to output projections specifically: Muon on q/k/v/c_fc ONLY and AdamW on the two c_proj groups. It has the SAME number of matrices moved and the same drop in orthogonalized share; if it moves val_bpb the same way, the mediator is merely 'fewer matrices on Muon' and the output-projection story is dead. A second, cheaper explanation is STEP COUNT: the arm removes 5 polar iterations on 14.68M parameters but adds two AdamW state tensors for them (~118 MB), so num_steps and step_ms_med must be read against the yoked control and any move beyond 1% step-law-corrected and flagged, per L005/L006.
falsifier: DID NOT ENGAGE (inconclusive, never a negative): muon_param_frac still prints 0.500005, or muon_group_count is unchanged, or moved_disp_ratio is below half the control's -- the q/k/v/c_fc matrices barely moved and the arm measured a partial freeze. ENGAGED AND DID NOTHING (kills the mechanism at this operating point): muon_param_frac 0.20833, moved_disp_ratio within 2x of the control's, num_steps within 1% of the yoked control, and val_bpb inside the wave's measured band -- which says the orthogonalized SHARE is flat here and that r23's Mamba-2 result does not carry to a transformer with value embeddings. ENGAGED AND HARMED beyond the band is not a null but positive evidence for r27_ns_orthogonalization_is_the_core (the polar iteration, not the momentum bookkeeping, is what carries Muon), and closes this direction downward rather than leaving it open.
mediator: The FRACTION OF THE PARAMETER BUDGET whose update direction is spectrally flattened (all singular values driven to 1 by the polar iteration) rather than left with the gradient's own per-coordinate anisotropy rescaled by Adam's second moment. At vocab 8192 this fraction is currently 0.500005 by construction: Muon owns c_q/c_k/c_v (6,291,456), attn.c_proj (2,097,152), mlp.c_fc (8,388,608), mlp.c_proj (8,388,608) and the four ve_gate matrices (512) = 25,166,336 of 50,332,176 parameters, while AdamW owns wte (4,194,304), lm_head (4,194,304) and value_embeds (16,777,216) = 25,165,824. Half this model has never seen Muon, and every imported Muon result speaks only to the other half. Restricting Muon to the two OUTPUT projections (attn.c_proj + mlp.c_proj = 10,485,760) moves the orthogonalized share to 0.20833. The physical distinction is not 'which optimizer' but WHICH DIRECTION A MATRIX FACES: c_q/c_k/c_v/c_fc READ the residual stream and inherit its per-channel scale, so flattening their spectrum destroys information the stream's own scale structure carries; c_proj matrices WRITE into the stream and have no such inherited scale, which is the class the 130M result singles out.
name: muon_scope_restricted_to_output_projections

activation_observable: nesterov_order_cos_med -- the median over sampled steps (every 32) of the cosine similarity between the update the treatment applies and the update the CONTROL ordering would have produced from the same momentum buffer, on one probe Muon group. Both are already available inside the step; the comparison costs one extra polar evaluation on the probe group only. ENGAGED means nesterov_order_cos_med < 0.99; a value above 0.999 means the reorder is algebraically near-inert at mu=0.95 and the run says nothing about the mechanism. Because a cosine is a ratio, per L014 it carries a companion SATURATION observable: nesterov_order_rms_ratio = median over the same samples of RMS(treatment update) / RMS(control-ordering update). The degeneracy it catches is the one that turns this into a knob -- lerp between two matrices with equal Frobenius norm can change the step LENGTH by up to (1+mu), so a value outside [0.95, 1.05] means the arm is a disguised learning-rate change and must be rebuilt with the length renormalized before it is scored. Both numbers are accumulated as 0-dim CUDA tensors appended to a Python list and .item()-ed only after the charged clock stops (the _mtp_hist pattern in tools/make_variant.py), and are computed in MuonAdamW._step_muon, OUTSIDE muon_step_fused, which is @torch.compile(dynamic=False, fullgraph=True): a reduction or print inside it graph-breaks or forces a recompile, and b1_optimizer_fusion_break_costs_loss records a pure-numerics loss regression from exactly that class of accident. Emit both in the CONTROL too (where cos is 1.0 and the ratio 1.0 by construction), so 'engaged' is a comparison rather than a bare number.
competing_explanation: AN EFFECTIVE LEARNING-RATE CHANGE, and here it is the default hypothesis rather than a remote one, because the reorder trivially rescales the update norm; nesterov_order_rms_ratio is built to be the discriminator and an arm whose ratio is 1.00 +/- 0.05 has by construction the same LR integral as its yoked control, leaving only the direction as a difference. A SECOND, sharper competing explanation is that the gain is not the ordering at all but the two-way LR scaling that r27_muon_symmetric_lr_scaling_gain reports from the SAME figure (16.60 -> 16.52), which in this codebase is the max(1.0, shape[-2]/shape[-1])**0.5 clamp in _step_muon and is already covered by the registered mechanism muon_shape_clamp_on_fan_in_heavy_matrices. The combined post-NS-Nesterov + symmetric-scaling number in that claim is 16.51, i.e. the ordering component is worth about 0.01 PPL on its own -- roughly 0.5% relative -- so the two must be run as SEPARATE arms and never bundled, or a win will be attributed to the wrong knob. Third: b0_adamuon_second_moment_on_ns_output_alone_hurts is direct opposing evidence that post-orthogonalization operations can be unstable elementwise; if this arm harms, that claim, not the ordering theory, is the likelier reading.
falsifier: DID NOT ENGAGE: nesterov_order_cos_med >= 0.999, or nesterov_order_rms_ratio outside [0.95, 1.05] (the arm changed step length, not order). Either makes the run inconclusive about the mechanism, per E3. ENGAGED AND DID NOTHING: cos in the 0.90-0.99 band, rms ratio within 5% of 1, num_steps within 0.5% of the yoked control, and val_bpb inside the measured band -- that closes the operator-ORDER axis at this horizon while leaving the operator-CONTENT axis (stateless_row_rms_normalization_before_polar) untouched, because the two are separate physical claims. A sharper kill: the effect appears at mu=0.95 but vanishes when the same reorder is run at mu=0.90 and mu=0.98, which would say the result is a momentum-constant artifact rather than an ordering effect.
mediator: WHERE the Nesterov lookahead extrapolation is formed relative to the polar iteration -- i.e. whether the extrapolated direction is built in GRADIENT space and then orthogonalized as one object (baseline: momentum_buffer.lerp_(stacked_grads, 1-mu); g = stacked_grads.lerp_(momentum_buffer, mu); then Newton-Schulz), or built between two matrices that have ALREADY been driven to flat spectra. The physical quantity is the angle on the manifold of orthogonal matrices between the applied update and the polar image of the current momentum. Pre-NS, the lookahead perturbs the INPUT of a scale- and (partly) shape-equivariant nonlinearity whose opening line X = X/(||X||*1.02+1e-6) and whose iteration renormalize away much of the perturbation; post-NS it is a fixed-angle extrapolation that the iteration can no longer absorb. This mechanism explicitly does NOT move the momentum accumulation: r27_muon_operator_order_constraint measures 16.60 -> 23.01 PPL when momentum is accumulated in orthogonalized space, and an audit of baseline/train.py confirms the baseline already satisfies both hard constraints in that claim -- momentum accumulates in gradient space, and the LR (including the shape factor) is applied post-NS in stacked_params.sub_(lr*g...). The lookahead position is the remaining degree of freedom the same figure measures as a GAIN.
name: nesterov_lookahead_after_orthogonalization

activation_observable: ve_over_wte_disp = ve_disp_ratio / wte_disp_ratio, where ve_disp_ratio = ||VE_final - VE_init||_F / ||VE_init||_F over the concatenated four value_embeds tables and wte_disp_ratio is the same for wte -- one clone of each at step 0, one difference at the end, both clones dropped, printed AFTER the charged clock stops. Emitted by EVERY arm including the control, so 'engaged' is a comparison: the control's value is whatever the shared LR and the two gradient geometries produce, and ENGAGED means the treatment's ve_over_wte_disp differs from its yoked control's by more than 40%. Because that is a ratio, per L014 it carries TWO companion floor/saturation observables. (a) ve_emb_rms_final, the RMS of the value_embeds weights, whose init value is known exactly: init_weights draws uniform(-s, s) with s = sqrt(3)*512**-0.5 = 0.076547, so RMS_init = 0.044194. A value collapsed toward 0 or run away past ~0.15 means the table was destroyed or saturated and the displacement ratio is meaningless. (b) ve_gate_w_absmean, the mean |ve_gate.weight| over the four VE-carrying layers, which is EXACTLY 0.0 at init by construction; a value near 0 means the gate never learned to route the tables at all, so a null about their learning rate says nothing. Both are single epilogue reductions, nothing inside the compiled step.
competing_explanation: AN EFFECTIVE LEARNING-RATE CHANGE -- trivially, since the intervention IS a learning rate. The mechanism is therefore not 'the LR moved' but 'the two tables want different LRs', and the DISCRIMINATOR is a third arm that scales BOTH groups by the same factor, covering the same range as the decoupled arms. If the global arm reproduces the best decoupled arm's val_bpb, the mediator is total embedding step size, the decoupling story is refuted, and what remains is an ordinary EMBEDDING_LR knob already inside the campaign's knob space. A SECOND, cheaper and easily missed explanation is NUMERIC, and it is specific to this codebase: init_weights casts wte and every value_embeds table to bf16, so an AdamW update smaller than half an ulp of a 0.044-scale bf16 weight (~2^-9 relative) is dropped entirely. Raising the VE learning rate could therefore win purely by escaping update underflow, not by any parameterization argument. Discriminating observation: ve_update_underflow_frac, the fraction of value_embeds entries whose |AdamW update| falls below half an ulp of the current weight, sampled every 32 steps and reduced after the clock stops. If it is materially above zero in the control and near zero in the treatment, the win is numeric and the fix is the dtype, not the LR. Third: any change to the value_embeds group also changes how much the zero-initialised ve_gate has to compensate, so ve_gate_w_absmean must be reported in both arms.
falsifier: DID NOT ENGAGE: ve_over_wte_disp within 40% of the yoked control's, or ve_gate_w_absmean below ~1e-4 (the tables were never routed), or ve_emb_rms_final outside [0.02, 0.15]. ENGAGED AND DID NOTHING: ve_over_wte_disp moved by more than 40% in BOTH directions across a two-sided pair of arms (ve LR raised, ve LR lowered), ve_emb_rms_final healthy in both, and val_bpb inside the measured band in both -- a two-sided null is what closes this axis, because a one-sided null is indistinguishable from having moved the wrong way. Note the direction the evidence predicts: r21_embedding_lr_matters_earliest_in_training reports a PERSISTENT 0.1-0.2 nat gap when the embedding LR is crippled EARLY, and at ~1010 steps this entire run is the early phase, so the asymmetry should be visible if it exists at all.
mediator: The RATIO of per-step relative displacement delivered to the two token-identity tables, which setup_optimizer currently forces to be driven by ONE scalar: both the wte group and the value_embeds group are constructed with lr = embedding_lr * (n_embd/768)**-0.5 = 0.6 * 1.224745 = 0.734847. At vocab 8192 these are not comparable objects. wte is 8192x512 = 4,194,304 parameters read once at the root of the residual stream; value_embeds is FOUR 8192x512 tables = 16,777,216 parameters, 33.33% of the whole model and 4x wte, injected into the attention VALUE path through a zero-initialised sigmoid gate. One scalar therefore sets the step size for 41.67% of the parameters, and the vocabulary that made that grouping conventional (50257) is not the vocabulary this model has. The mediator is the displacement ratio itself, not the LR: the claim under test is that the input map and the value map want DIFFERENT step sizes, and r21_embedding_lr_is_primary_driver_of_mup_advantage is a full LRxWDxwidthxparameterization grid (internal validity 4) saying a Theta(1) embedding LR is the SINGLE change that makes standard parameterization match muP.
name: embedding_lr_decoupled_from_value_embeddings

activation_observable: ve_emb_rms_final and wte_rms_final, two epilogue reductions with EXACTLY known references: value_embeds init uniform(-0.076547, 0.076547) gives RMS_init = 0.044194, and wte init normal(0, 1) gives RMS_init = 1.0. ENGAGED means ve_emb_rms_final at least 5% below the yoked control's value. The interesting quantity ve_emb_rms_final / 0.044194 is a ratio, so per L014 it carries a companion SHAPE observable that distinguishes real regularization from a uniform rescale: ve_row_rms_ratio_p99_p50, the 99th over the 50th percentile of per-ROW RMS across the 8192 rows of the concatenated tables. Uniform shrinkage of an already-isotropic table moves the LEVEL and leaves this ratio unchanged -- that outcome is an effective-LR change wearing a decay label, not shrinkage doing regularization work, and it is the degeneracy that would otherwise make ve_emb_rms_final meaningless. Print wd_by_group alongside them, the list of weight_decay values actually held by each of the five AdamW groups at the end of the run, so 'two groups changed' is distinguishable from 'a module constant changed all five'. All three are computed after the charged clock stops; nothing is added inside adamw_step_fused, which is @torch.compile(fullgraph=True).
competing_explanation: AN EFFECTIVE LEARNING-RATE REDUCTION. Decoupled decay on a table whose update is already normalized by Adam's second moment is close to a uniform multiplicative shrink, i.e. a smaller effective step, and this campaign carries a registered claim (o0_mgup_gain_confounded_by_effective_lr) about exactly this confusion. TWO DISCRIMINATORS. (1) LR-MATCHED ARM: leave weight_decay at 0.0 and instead lower EMBEDDING_LR by the factor that reproduces the treatment's measured ve_emb_rms_final; if it reproduces val_bpb, this is step size. (2) ve_row_rms_ratio_p99_p50, which is shape rather than level -- an LR change cannot compress the tail of the per-row norm distribution, and decay that is doing regularization work must. A second competing explanation is CAPACITY REMOVAL: shrinking a third of the model's parameters toward zero is, at the limit, r21_freezing_embedding_hurts_more_under_mup's frozen-embedding arm, which hurt at every width; so a two-sided sweep is required and a monotone 'more decay is worse' response is evidence that the mechanism is capacity, not overfitting control. A third: b1_indep_wd_scales_inverse_width says independent weight decay must be scaled with width, so the chosen constant is not portable from any cited paper and must be swept, not copied.
falsifier: DID NOT ENGAGE: wd_by_group shows the intended groups still at 0.0, or ve_emb_rms_final within 5% of the yoked control's (the decay was too small to bind at this horizon -- note AdamW here applies p.mul_(1 - lr*wd) with lr 0.734847, so wd and lr multiply and a nominal wd looks much larger than it does on the Muon groups). ENGAGED AND DID NOTHING: ve_emb_rms_final at least 5% below control, ve_row_rms_ratio_p99_p50 also reduced, num_steps within 1%, and val_bpb inside the measured band. PRECONDITION FAILURE, which is a third and distinct outcome: b0_moonlight_weight_decay_helps_only_when_overtrained reports that Muon WITHOUT decay converged FASTER early and that decay only paid in the over-trained regime, so if final_epoch in this wave is below ~1.5 the regime the mechanism needs is absent and a null is inconclusive rather than negative; final_epoch must be read before the verdict.
mediator: The WEIGHT-NORM TRAJECTORY of the 41.67% of parameters that currently receive no shrinkage of any kind. All five AdamW groups in setup_optimizer are constructed with weight_decay=0.0, while WEIGHT_DECAY=0.2 -- and it is a cautious, sign-masked decay, applied only where update and parameter agree in sign -- reaches only the Muon groups. Regularization therefore touches 25,166,336 parameters and misses 25,165,824, of which value_embeds alone is 16,777,216. The physical quantity is the end-of-run per-row norm of the token-identity tables, which sets how confidently a single token id can dominate the attention value path. Vocab 8192 is what makes this a live lever rather than a transplanted convention: at 524,288 tokens/step and ~1010 steps each of the 8192 rows is touched ~6.5e4 times on average, so these tables sit at the opposite end of the axis r27_large_embedding_tables_get_sparse_updates measures (7.3% of rows getting >100 updates at 2M vocab). They are dense-update, high-capacity, and unshrunk, in a frame that sits at the ~2-epoch boundary of a fixed dataset.
name: decay_on_the_token_identity_tables

activation_observable: zloss_frac_of_total = ZLOSS_W * logz_sq_mean / mean(train_loss), together with logz_sq_mean itself -- BOTH ALREADY EMITTED by the cfg['zloss'] branch of tools/make_variant.py, accumulated in _zl_sum on device and converted only in the epilogue. ENGAGED at lambda=1e-1 means zloss_frac_of_total > 0.01, i.e. the term is at least 1% of the objective; at lambda=1e-4 the same branch is expected to print below 1e-5, and that number IS the registered null, which is why 1e-4 must never be run as the treatment arm. THE YOKED CONTROL MUST BE BUILT WITH zloss=0.0, not as the plain control: cfg.get('zloss') is not None passes at 0.0, so the control emits the same logz_sq_mean, is charged the same chunked logsumexp, and differs from the treatment only in the coefficient. Because zloss_frac_of_total is a ratio, per L014 it carries a companion SATURATION observable: logit_softcap_sat_frac, the fraction of pre-cap |logits| above the 15 knee, sampled every 32 steps on a slice and reduced after the clock stops. If the softcap is already saturating a material share of logits, log Z is pinned by tanh and z-loss has no free direction left to act on -- the term would be present, its share nonzero, and the mechanism nonetheless unable to engage. Emit logit_softcap_sat_frac in both arms.
competing_explanation: LEARNING-RATE HEADROOM, NOT PARTITION CONTROL, and this is not a speculative alternative -- it is what the source paper actually measured. r22_logit_regularizers_only_buy_lr_headroom reports the benefit as a 3x drop in LR sensitivity (109M LRS 0.344 -> 0.118) with the optimal loss UNCHANGED at 3.20, and the -0.02-nat figure at lambda=1e-1 is a best-over-seven-learning-rates column. So a gain here is most cheaply read as 'the fixed LRs happened to sit closer to their optimum once the logits were regularized'. DISCRIMINATOR: run lambda=1e-1 at the baseline LRs AND at a second point with UNEMBEDDING_LR and EMBEDDING_LR both raised 1.5x. If the gain appears only at the raised LR, the mediator is headroom and the correct intervention is the learning rate, not the loss term. SECOND, THROUGHPUT: the chunked logsumexp is a second full pass over a [B*T, 8192] tensor; r22_output_embedding_centering_is_near_free measured z-loss at +1.5% training time at 109M with vocab 50304, and at vocab 8192 the vocab-projection share of the step is much smaller, so the percentage must be re-measured, not assumed. Building the control at zloss=0.0 charges that cost to both arms and removes the confound entirely, which is why that control is mandatory rather than optional. THIRD: mu-centering was the near-free variant but NOT the one that lowered optimal loss, so a win must not be generalized to 'logit regularization helps'.
falsifier: DID NOT ENGAGE: zloss_frac_of_total below 1e-3 (the coefficient did not reach the objective), or logit_softcap_sat_frac materially above zero in the CONTROL, which means tanh already owns the quantity z-loss is meant to control and the run is inconclusive. ENGAGED AND DID NOTHING: zloss_frac_of_total > 0.01, logz_sq_mean measurably lower than the zloss=0.0 control's, logit_softcap_sat_frac ~0 in both, num_steps within 1%, and val_bpb inside the measured band -- which closes logit-partition control as a bpb lever at vocab 8192 and at ~1010 steps, and is exactly what r27_output_logit_divergence_not_reproduced and r27_softmax_collapse_in_gpt_training predict at this scale and horizon. A sweep that shows val_bpb monotone in lambda over {1e-2, 1e-1, 1} with no interior optimum would also kill it, because the mechanism's own evidence says the window is interior.
mediator: The VARIANCE OF log Z = logsumexp(logits) ACROSS TOKEN POSITIONS -- the single direction in logit space that the cross-entropy gradient is blind to, because softmax is invariant to adding a constant to every logit. z-loss is the only term that penalizes drift along it. Vocab 8192 changes the accounting twice. The normalizer is a sum over 6.1x fewer terms than in every paper that measured z-loss, and the entropy ceiling is ln(8192) = 9.0109 rather than ln(50257) = 10.8246, so log Z has both less to sum and less room to wander. Separately, the baseline ALREADY applies a softcap, logits = 15*tanh(logits/15) at line 292, which pins the logit RANGE; what z-loss can still add is control of the MEAN LEVEL. The lambda that matters is 1e-1, not the conventional 1e-4: r22_zloss_lambda_default_does_not_improve_loss is an exact null at 1e-4 (109M: 3.20 both arms) and r22_zloss_lambda_0p1_lowers_optimal_loss reports -0.02 nats at 1e-1 at the same 109M FineWeb cell, which is roughly 0.007 bpb, while r22_zloss_large_lambda_catastrophic puts 1e2 at 3.64. The usable window is narrow and known.
name: logit_partition_control_at_hundredfold_lambda

activation_observable: mir_mask_frac_realized -- the measured fraction of input positions actually replaced by the mask id, averaged over steps. With the source's r_min=0, r_max=0.5 and r ~ U(r_min, r_max) drawn per batch, ENGAGED means mir_mask_frac_realized in [0.20, 0.30]; anything near 0 says the corruption never applied. Read it with mir_aux_loss_drop = (mean auxiliary CE over the first 100 steps) - (mean over the last 100), ENGAGED means > 0.1, accumulated as 0-dim CUDA tensors in a Python list and .item()-ed only after the charged clock stops, the _mtp_hist pattern already in tools/make_variant.py. The share quantity mir_aux_share = lambda*aux/(aux + train_loss) is a ratio, so per L014 it carries a companion FLOOR: mir_aux_loss_final read against ln(8192) = 9.0109. An auxiliary loss sitting within ~0.2 of 9.0109 means the corrupted view carries no usable signal at this vocabulary and the term is a pure gradient-noise injector -- the share can be large while the mechanism is entirely absent, which is precisely the case the floor catches. num_steps and vram_reserved_mb are also part of the activation test for this mechanism, not merely diagnostics. IMPLEMENTATION CONSTRAINT: prepare.py is frozen at VOCAB_SIZE=8192 and has no MASK id, so the mask must be ONE extra learned row on the INPUT side only -- wte becomes nn.Embedding(8193, 512), +512 parameters -- with lm_head left at 8192 so targets, the evaluator and the BPB byte accounting are untouched; the auxiliary pass must be gated on self.training so evaluate_bpb's path stays bit-identical, exactly as the mtp branch is.
competing_explanation: THROUGHPUT, and here it dominates the science. A second forward and backward on the same 128x2048 micro-batch roughly doubles the compute per step, and the campaign's step law converts a step-count loss straight into bpb, so the cheapest explanation of a LOSS is 'it bought fewer steps' and of a WIN is nothing at all until step count is matched. Discriminating observations in order: num_steps and step_ms_med against the yoked control -- any drop beyond 1% forces a step-law-corrected, flagged verdict rather than a pooled one -- then vram_reserved_mb, because the second pass materializes another [128*2048, 8192] logits tensor, 4.29 GB in bf16 and 8.59 GB after the baseline's logits.float(), so an allocator regime change (expandable-segment thrash or OOM) is a cheaper explanation than supervision density for anything anomalous. SECOND COMPETING EXPLANATION, and the cheaper implementation that must be ruled out before paying for a second pass: corrupt a fraction of positions in the SINGLE existing forward and keep the loss on all positions. That costs zero extra FLOPs and delivers input-corruption regularization without the second view. If the cheap arm reproduces the effect, the mediator is input noise, not supervision density, and the second pass should never be paid for. THIRD: o2_namo_train_loss_gain_is_ten_times_its_val_loss_gain is the reason train_loss must not be scored here -- an auxiliary term that lowers train loss by 0.1 bought only 0.008-0.019 val at 124M.
falsifier: DID NOT ENGAGE: mir_mask_frac_realized outside [0.20, 0.30], or mir_aux_loss_final within 0.2 of 9.0109 (the auxiliary task is at the uniform-prediction floor), or mir_aux_loss_drop below 0.1. ENGAGED AND DID NOTHING: mask fraction in band, aux loss well below 9.0 and falling, and val_bpb inside the yoked band AT EQUAL STEP COUNT. PRECONDITION FAILURE, reported separately: the source result is from a DATA-CONSTRAINED repeated-epoch regime against a strongly regularized tuned baseline; if final_epoch in this wave is below ~1.5 the regime is absent and a null is inconclusive. MAGNITUDE WARNING that governs the design: at 72M the measured gain was 3.615903 -> 3.613621, i.e. 0.0023 nats, only rising to ~0.03 at 1.4B. At 50.33M the predicted effect is at or below the campaign's resolution, so a single yoked pair CANNOT falsify this mechanism; it needs n>=3 with the token-law control variate, and a one-pair null must be recorded as underpowered rather than negative.
mediator: The number of INDEPENDENT SUPERVISED GRADIENTS EXTRACTED PER TOKEN OF DATA, as opposed to per forward pass. A second forward on a [MASK]-corrupted copy of the SAME batch adds a next-token loss whose conditioning set is a random subset of the context, so it supervises prediction from partial evidence and consumes no new tokens. That is the axis that matters at this operating point specifically: ~94% of charged time is the frozen single-threaded packing loop, so GPU FLOPs are the cheap resource and unique tokens are the scarce one, and the 300s frame sits near the 2-epoch boundary of a fixed dataset. It is distinct from the registered mtp_supervision_density mechanism, which adds a SECOND HEAD on the SAME activations at a different target offset (more targets per representation); this adds a SECOND VIEW of the same data through the same head (more representations per target).
name: masked_input_auxiliary_pass

activation_observable: ns_input_row_rms_cv -- the coefficient of variation (std/mean) across rows of the per-row RMS of the tensor ACTUALLY handed to the polar loop, averaged over Muon groups and over steps sampled every 32. ENGAGED means the treatment prints below 0.02, since row normalization drives it to 0 up to epsilon; the control prints the untouched momentum's value. Because a CV is a ratio, per L014 it carries a companion FLOOR observable computed in BOTH arms on the momentum BEFORE any normalization: momentum_row_rms_cv. If the control's momentum_row_rms_cv is itself below ~0.1 there was no heterogeneity to remove, the treatment is a no-op by construction, and a null is a non-activation rather than a negative -- that is the degeneracy the ratio alone cannot show. Also print rownorm_eps_clamp_frac, the fraction of rows whose RMS fell below the epsilon and were therefore left un-normalized or amplified; the precond arm's silent failure was exactly a clamp binding while its declared activation test passed, so a floor-binding fraction is now mandatory alongside any ratio. Finally print rownorm_reduce_dim per group, the integer reduction dim actually used: for an nn.Linear weight stored [d_out, d_in] the per-output-neuron normalization reduces over dim -1, and o2_muoneq_rownorm_before_ns_beats_muon_at_130m records that the transposed orientation was the WORST of the three variants tested. The existing NorMuon block picks red_dim = -1 if shape[-2] >= shape[-1] else -2, which is SHAPE-based and would silently flip the orientation on the (512, 2048) mlp.c_proj group, so this dim must be pinned to -1 for every group and printed. All observables are computed in MuonAdamW._step_muon or the epilogue, OUTSIDE muon_step_fused, which is @torch.compile(dynamic=False, fullgraph=True).
competing_explanation: AN EFFECTIVE LEARNING-RATE CHANGE, with an unusually strong structural argument against it that must nonetheless be CHECKED rather than assumed: the polar iteration's opening line divides by the Frobenius norm, X = X/(||X||*1.02 + 1e-6), so any purely GLOBAL rescale of the input is cancelled exactly and cannot survive as a step-size change. What can survive is a change in the update's post-iteration magnitude arising from the changed spectrum. The discriminating observable is ns_output_rms_ratio = RMS(post-NS update, treatment) / RMS(post-NS update, control ordering) on a probe group; orthogonalization should make it ~1 if the mechanism acts on direction alone, and any value outside [0.95, 1.05] requires an LR-matched arm before the result is scored. SECOND COMPETING EXPLANATION -- the one that already cost this campaign a run -- is DEGENERACY: dividing a near-zero row by its own RMS amplifies pure noise into the iteration, so the arm could 'win' or 'lose' entirely through noise injection on dead rows; rownorm_eps_clamp_frac is what makes that visible, and it must be near zero for any verdict to stand. THIRD, THROUGHPUT: two extra reductions per group per step. The edit itself must stay INSIDE muon_step_fused (it is elementwise plus a reduction and compiles cleanly) while the observables stay outside, because b1_optimizer_fusion_break_costs_loss records a pure-numerics loss regression caused by breaking that fused update rather than by any algorithmic change. FOURTH: r27_ns_orthogonalization_is_the_core says the orthogonalization itself carries Muon and that pre/post decorations are secondary (16.86 -> 16.76 -> 16.60), so the prior on effect size is small and n=1 cannot resolve it.
falsifier: DID NOT ENGAGE: ns_input_row_rms_cv above 0.02 in the treatment, or rownorm_eps_clamp_frac above ~0.01 (the epsilon is binding and the arm is the L014 failure again in a new costume), or rownorm_reduce_dim not -1 on every group (the arm ran the known-worst orientation and its result bears on that, not on this mechanism), or momentum_row_rms_cv below 0.1 in the CONTROL (nothing to remove). ENGAGED AND DID NOTHING: ns_input_row_rms_cv < 0.02, rownorm_eps_clamp_frac ~0, dim -1 everywhere, momentum_row_rms_cv comfortably above 0.1 in the control, num_steps within 0.5%, and val_bpb inside the measured band -- that is a real negative and it closes pre-polar input conditioning as a family, which precond_before_ortho's run could not do because it never engaged.
mediator: The PER-ROW RMS HETEROGENEITY of the momentum matrix at the instant it enters the polar iteration -- which singular directions the iteration is asked to equalize. This is deliberately the same mediator as the registered mechanism precond_before_ortho, and the point of registering it separately is the distinction L014 forced: precond_before_ortho fed the NorMuon EMA BUFFER with raw momentum, whose entries are orders of magnitude smaller than orthogonalized entries, so 99.8% of the buffer sat on clamp_min(1e-10), the diagonal collapsed to a constant, the polar iteration's own X = X/(||X||*1.02+1e-6) cancelled it exactly, and the arm silently ran as plain-Muon-minus-NorMuon. This mechanism is STATELESS: divide each row of the momentum by its own RMS this step. No buffer, no EMA, no missing bias correction, and no absolute floor to fall through -- the only degeneracy left is a genuinely near-zero row, which an explicit epsilon and its own observable cover. The physical claim being separated out is that the heterogeneity worth removing is INSTANTANEOUS and per-output-neuron, not an accumulated second moment.
name: stateless_row_rms_normalization_before_polar

activation_observable: logz_sq_final -- mean of (logsumexp over vocab)^2 averaged over the LAST 10% of training steps, emitted by EVERY arm including the control. The last-10% window is essential: a whole-run average is dominated by the log(8192)=9.0 transient at initialisation (log^2 Z = 81) and would read high even in an arm where the regularizer worked perfectly, which is exactly the ratio-with-no-floor-companion failure L014 was written about. Companion: zloss_frac_of_total (lambda * logz^2 / total loss), which separates 'the term is present and material' from 'lambda was too small to matter' -- the registered null at lambda=1e-4 is precisely the second case.
competing_explanation: AN EFFECTIVE LOGIT-SCALE OR LEARNING-RATE CHANGE ON THE UNEMBEDDING. Penalising log^2 Z applies a large, nearly uniform downward gradient to every logit, which shrinks the lm_head and is equivalent to lowering the effective logit temperature; the model already carries a 15*tanh(z/15) softcap that does the same job by a different route, so a win could be pure logit-scale tuning. Discriminating observations: (1) the existing `softcap` knob is a same-cost arm that changes logit scale WITHOUT constraining log Z -- if moving softcap reproduces the gain, the mechanism is logit scale and not partition regularisation; (2) logz_sq_final must fall by an order of magnitude while zloss_frac_of_total ends small, i.e. the term did its work and then got out of the way, rather than the loss being reduced by trading CE for a shrinking penalty term.
falsifier: ENGAGED-AND-INERT: logz_sq_final is driven below 1.0 while the yoked control's sits an order of magnitude higher, and val_bpb is inside the counterbalanced resolution. That means pinning the partition function buys nothing at 1010 steps, which is the reading two registered claims already predict (the measured benefit of these regularizers was learning-rate headroom, not a lower optimal loss, and at a low base LR all logit interventions were a wash). DID-NOT-ENGAGE: zloss_frac_of_total is under 0.01, i.e. the term never became a material part of the objective -- inconclusive. ENGAGED-AND-DESTRUCTIVE, which is a different verdict from inert: logz_sq_final near 0 with val_bpb worse than the control by more than 0.005 reproduces the catastrophic-lambda regime one size down and bounds the usable band from above.
mediator: the magnitude of the logit partition function log Z = logsumexp(logits) in steady state. Cross-entropy is exactly invariant to a uniform shift of the logits, so nothing in the baseline objective constrains log Z at all: the uniform component of the unembedding is a free direction that the optimizer wanders along. Adding lambda * (log Z)^2 makes that direction the only one the extra term acts on, pinning log Z near 0 and removing a degree of freedom that otherwise consumes unembedding capacity and lm_head gradient variance -- the lm_head is the highest-gradient-variance tensor in the model. MERGED WITH logit_partition_control_at_hundredfold_lambda: Both name the same intervention (z-loss at a large coefficient) and cite the same claims. The implemented penalty is mean(logsumexp^2), which equals var + mean^2, so no run can separate 'magnitude of log Z' from 'variance of log Z across positions' -- they are one bet.
merge_note: Both name the same intervention (z-loss at a large coefficient) and cite the same claims. The implemented penalty is mean(logsumexp^2), which equals var + mean^2, so no run can separate 'magnitude of log Z' from 'variance of log Z across positions' -- they are one bet.

activation_observable: muon_param_frac -- Muon-owned parameters divided by all 2D parameters in transformer.h, printed by EVERY arm (control reads 1.000000). Companion observables, both required because the ratio alone cannot distinguish a reassignment from a de-facto learning-rate change: muon_upd_rms_med, the median per-entry RMS of the update applied to the matrices Muon still owns, and adamw_hidden_upd_rms_med, the same statistic for the matrices just demoted to AdamW. The demotion is only an assignment test if the second is within a factor of two of what Muon was delivering to those tensors in the control.
competing_explanation: A LEARNING-RATE FIT, not an assignment effect. The source paper re-tuned per-group learning rates separately in every assignment regime, so its 0.045-nat gap bundles assignment with LR search; and our demoted matrices have no tuned AdamW learning rate at all -- they inherit whatever we pick. A registered claim (o2_muon_hybrid_beats_adamw_at_shared_untuned_lr) says an untuned shared LR favours the Muon hybrid, so an untuned demotion is expected to lose for reasons that have nothing to do with assignment. Discriminating observation: choose the demoted groups' AdamW LR by RMS matching to the Muon update those exact tensors received in the control (MATRIX_LR * shape_factor / sqrt(max(m,n))), and put muon_upd_rms_med and adamw_hidden_upd_rms_med on the record so the match is checkable rather than asserted.
falsifier: ENGAGED-AND-WRONG: muon_param_frac drops from 1.0 to ~0.42, the demoted matrices are demonstrably being stepped by AdamW at an update RMS within a factor of two of the Muon update they replaced (muon_upd_rms_med and adamw_hidden_upd_rms_med bracket each other), and val_bpb is inside the counterbalanced resolution of the yoked control or worse. That says the assignment carries no information at this operating point and the whole restricted-assignment direction is dead here. DID-NOT-ENGAGE: muon_param_frac still reads 1.0, or the demoted groups' update RMS is off by an order of magnitude, which makes the arm an untuned-learning-rate experiment rather than an assignment experiment -- inconclusive, rerun with the RMS matched.
mediator: WHICH of a block's 2D matrices receive a spectral (orthogonalized) update rather than a coordinate-wise adaptive one. Muon's polar iteration equalizes the singular spectrum of whatever matrix it is handed; that is the right conditioning for a matrix whose job is to READ a d_model-dimensional residual stream and write back into it (attn.c_proj, mlp.c_proj), and the wrong one for matrices whose rows serve functionally heterogeneous roles or whose fan-in/fan-out are strongly unbalanced (c_q/c_k/c_v feeding 4 separate heads, mlp.c_fc feeding a squared-ReLU nonlinearity). Our stack hands Muon ALL transformer.h 2D parameters, i.e. 100% of 25.17M matrix parameters; the mediator is the fraction and identity of that set. MERGED WITH muon_scope_restricted_to_output_projections: Same intervention (Muon retained only on the output projections, other 2D matrices demoted to AdamW), same activation observable muon_param_frac, and a shared source claim.
merge_note: Same intervention (Muon retained only on the output projections, other 2D matrices demoted to AdamW), same activation observable muon_param_frac, and a shared source claim.
name: muon_assignment_by_projection_role_merged

activation_observable: secmom_ortho_ratio, which must fall far below 1 to show the buffer left orthogonalized scale, AND secmom_clamp_frac, which must stay near 0 to show it did not fall off the bottom instead. Either alone is insufficient: the ratio rule passed on all three non-engaged runs.
competing_explanation: an effective learning-rate change. Renormalizing the momentum before orthogonalization alters the norm of the matrix fed to the polar iteration, and the iteration's output scale is set by that input; so a win could be nothing but a global step-size change that the same wave would reproduce by moving lr alone. This must be ruled out with an LR-matched arm or by showing the post-NS RMS is preserved. NEW OPPOSING EVIDENCE, registered after the run: a transfer-4 claim from a paper measured at 124M-class scale and exactly 524288 tokens/step reports row-wise second-moment normalization working BETTER after Newton-Schulz than before, which is the baseline's ordering. This mechanism is now a contested bet rather than a favoured one, and a null from the corrected implementation should be read as corroborating that claim.
falsifier: val_bpb of the reordered variant is within the measured within-wave band of its yoked control WHILE the activation observable shows the preconditioner is materially non-identity (pre-NS entrywise rescale ratio far from 1). That combination says the intervention engaged and did nothing. If instead the observable shows the rescale ratio sitting at ~1, the run is INCONCLUSIVE about the mechanism, not evidence against it.
measured_outcome: NOT REFUTED -- NOT ENGAGED. Three runs (precond_pre_slot0, precond_pre_slot1, precond_pre_R1P_C) reported secmom_clamp_frac 0.99789, 0.99791 and 0.99791 against 0.00000 in every yoked control, so 99.8% of the second-moment buffer sat at the clamp_min(1e-10) floor and the arm ran as plain Muon minus NorMuon. The val_bpb deltas (+0.001288, -0.000433, +0.000809) are therefore INCONCLUSIVE about this mechanism. See L014_precond_clamped_out_did_not_engage.
mediator: the entrywise scale distribution of the momentum matrix AT THE MOMENT it enters Newton-Schulz. Orthogonalization is scale-equivariant in a way that discards entrywise second-moment information: normalizing the momentum by its running second moment BEFORE the polar iteration changes which singular directions the iteration is asked to equalize, whereas the same normalization applied AFTER only rescales an already-orthogonalized update and cannot change its direction. IMPLEMENTATION CORRECTED: the momentum is now rescaled to unit RMS per matrix before the second moment is taken, which puts the buffer back in the range its floor and zero-init were designed for. The rescale is a per-matrix scalar and the polar iteration opens by dividing by the Frobenius norm, so it cannot smuggle in an effective learning-rate change. MERGED WITH stateless_row_rms_normalization_before_polar: The latter's own mediator text says it is deliberately the same mediator: reshaping the row scale of the momentum before the polar iteration. Stateless-vs-EMA is a parameter of one mechanism, not two mechanisms, and running them in separate waves would be one bet placed twice.

activation_observable: gpu_slack_frac = 1 - gpu_span_ms_med / step_ms_med, printed by EVERY arm including the control, alongside gpu_span_ms_med. gpu_span_ms is measured with a pair of torch.cuda.Event(enable_timing=True) recorded at the top of the micro-step loop and after optimizer.step(); recording an event does not synchronize, and elapsed_time is queried for all steps only AFTER the charged clock stops, so the instrument cannot move val_bpb or the step count (2 events x ~1015 steps is negligible). Values: gpu_slack_frac > 0.1 means the free-FLOPs regime holds for this run; ~0 means the GPU is the critical path and every FLOP added from here is paid for at the step law's exchange rate of -0.063 to -0.0687 bpb per e-fold of steps. The existing loader_frac telemetry is NOT sufficient for this: it measures CPU time inside next(train_loader), which overlaps GPU execution by construction and therefore cannot tell idleness from overlap.
competing_explanation: HOST CPU CONTENTION, which sets the packing time and is the dominant nuisance on this shared 192-core box: byte-identical control code has ranged 621 to 1021 steps, and L006 shows even the taskset core block moves the packing loop by 2.43 ms/step. Slack is therefore a property of the run's host load, not a constant of the system -- and it moves the FLATTERING way, since heavier host load slows packing and makes GPU work look freer. A treatment that appears free may simply have landed in a high-contention wave. Discriminating observations: read gpu_slack_frac off the yoked control of the SAME wave rather than from any earlier run; require the counterbalanced slot swap of L013 on the same 96-107/108-119 core pair; and report the treatment's added FLOPs as a fraction of the CONTROL's gpu_span_ms_med, so the headroom claim is stated against a concurrently measured denominator.
falsifier: ENGAGED-AND-WRONG (kills the mechanism): an arm that raises gpu_span_ms_med by 20% or more also raises step_ms_med by a comparable fraction, in a run whose measured gpu_slack_frac was above 0.3. That would mean the slack is not spendable -- most likely because the binding CPU cost is kernel-LAUNCH time in the main thread rather than GPU execution, in which case adding operations costs launches and the whole 'GPU capacity is free' framing of this campaign is wrong. DID-NOT-ENGAGE: gpu_span_ms_med does not move when FLOPs are added, meaning the FLOPs were never added or the events are timing an already-drained queue -- re-run, score nothing. NOTE the asymmetry that makes this mechanism useful: a FLOP-adding arm whose gpu_span_ms_med rises while step_ms_med and num_steps stay inside the yoked control's band CONFIRMS it, whatever val_bpb does. val_bpb is not this mechanism's endpoint; wall-clock price is.
mediator: The per-step overlap slack between the asynchronous GPU queue and the synchronous single-threaded CPU packing loop: slack_ms = step_ms - gpu_span_ms. The training loop calls next(train_loader) AFTER loss.backward() inside the gradient-accumulation loop (baseline/train.py:553-559) with no synchronization until train_loss.item(), so the CPU packs micro-batch k+1 while the GPU executes micro-batch k, and the step costs max(CPU, GPU) rather than their sum. With loader_frac measured around 0.94 of charged time, the GPU is the shorter leg by an order of magnitude, and the mediator is how much GPU work can be added before it stops being. This mechanism prices FLOPs; it does not promise loss. Its two directional consequences are what make it worth a record: added GPU work is free in wall-clock until the slack is consumed, and removed GPU work buys nothing -- which is exactly what L011 measured when 40% fewer Newton-Schulz iterations returned 0.2% of step time. MERGED WITH flop_slack_exchange_rate: Both propose to price GPU work against step time and both hinge on gpu_slack_frac. L019 has since measured the premise directly -- mfu is ~42.6%, so the GPU is substantially busy -- which collapses the two into a single question: what does a FLOP cost in steps.
