notes: NOT implemented -- new instrumentation only, no math change, and it belongs in the shared telemetry block of tools/make_variant.py so the control emits it too. It touches nothing inside muon_step_fused. This mechanism is the price sheet the other five need: periln_branch_output_norm, qk_norm_pins_attention_logit_scale and mtp_supervision_density all change GPU work, and none of their val_bpb deltas can be separated from the step law without it. Note also that tools/direction.py registers 'prefetch' as the input_pipeline mechanism, which attacks the SAME quantity from the other side (reclaiming the GPU-serialized remainder) and is bounded by it: with gpu_slack_frac near 0.9 the entire prize for perfect overlap is the ~10% GPU share, whereas the slack available to SPEND is nine times larger. prefetch is also, as of this record, not implemented in tools/make_variant.py at all.

activation_observable: num_steps, read against the yoked same-wave control on the paired GPU. The mechanism is a TRADE, so its activation is the throughput leg specifically, not val_bpb -- a run whose step count did not move has not exercised the trade and is INCONCLUSIVE about it regardless of where val_bpb landed. Unlike secmom_ortho_ratio, which turned out to be a path constant bit-identical across arms, num_steps demonstrably varies run to run (975 to 1022 across completed results), so it can actually discriminate.
competing_explanation: HOST CPU CONTENTION setting the step count through the frozen packing loop, which is the dominant nuisance on this shared 192-core box and moves step count far more than any attention edit will. Byte-identical control code has ranged 621 to 1021 steps across waves. This is ruled out, not by argument, but by the design: treatment and control run CONCURRENTLY in the same wave on paired GPUs, and the treatment occupies every GPU exactly once across the quad, so a device's fixed offset cancels rather than being absorbed into the effect. A second competing explanation is that the short span was never actually load-bearing at this sequence length, in which case the arm would show a step gain at essentially zero quality cost -- a real win, but attributable to the span having been oversized to begin with rather than to any favourable exchange rate.
falsifier: A shorter short-span that completes NO more steps than its yoked control. That would show attention FLOPs are not on the critical path at this operating point, and the whole exchange this mechanism describes does not exist here -- which is exactly what happened to the ns=3 arm, where a compute reduction worth ~0.2% of step time bought no measurable throughput and the arm came back WORSE by +0.002645. The second falsifier is a step gain that arrives with a val_bpb LOSS exceeding what the step law says those steps are worth, which would mean local context is load-bearing and the trade is simply bad.
mediator: The per-token attention FLOPs contributed by the SHORT-window layers of the SSSL pattern, which is linear in the short span. Halving the span halves those layers' attention cost, and the mediator is realised as num_steps completed inside the fixed 300-charged-second budget.
name: local_span_buys_steps

activation_observable: ve_share_by_layer: for each VE-carrying layer, the epilogue prints mean_over(tokens, kv_heads) of ||gate_l*ve_l||_2 / ||c_v(x)_l||_2 on one held-out eval batch, plus the scalars ve_share_min, ve_share_max and ve_share_spread = max/min. Emitted by BOTH arms of the yoked pair so 'engaged' is a comparison, not an assertion: the control prints it over its 4 layers, the treatment over 8. Companion floor observable ve_gate_w_absmean (min over VE layers of mean|ve_gate.weight|), which is EXACTLY 0.0 at step 0 by construction, so any value above ~1e-4 proves the gates learned rather than sitting at the neutral 1.0 they start at. All computed after the charged clock stops.
competing_explanation: The stride-1 arm simply holds 4 more vocab-sized tables (4 * 8192 * 256 more parameters plus their AdamW state) than the control. Any val_bpb movement could be raw capacity, or the step count those parameters cost inside the 300s budget, with the per-layer share doing no work at all. Ruling this out needs the share to differ across depth AND the fixed-share arm to differ from the decayed-share arm at matched parameter count.
falsifier: The stride-1 arm's measured ve_share_by_layer comes out FLAT across depth at end of training (max/min within 1.3x), AND an arm that explicitly imposes a 1/sqrt(l) decay on the injected term lands within the measured noise band of the un-decayed stride-1 arm. Then the share is not what the placement is acting through and this mechanism is dead regardless of which arm wins.
mediator: The per-layer share the injected value embedding takes of the value stream it is added to: mean over tokens and kv-heads of ||gate_l * ve_l|| / ||c_v(x)_l||. Adding a table at a layer sets this share from zero to order one there (ve_gate.weight inits to EXACTLY zero, so gate = 2*sigmoid(0) = 1.0, and value_embeds and c_v share the same uniform(-sqrt(3)/sqrt(512), +) init, so the injected term arrives at full strength, not switched off). A depth-decayed or per-layer-learned scale is an intervention on exactly this quantity, and the literature says a fixed-magnitude write buys less rotation the deeper the stream it enters.
name: ve_injection_share_of_value_stream

activation_observable: ve_disp_by_table: for each table, ||VE_i_final - VE_i_init||_F / ||VE_i_init||_F, computed from one step-0 clone per table dropped after the difference. The init reference is known exactly (uniform(-0.076547, 0.076547), RMS 0.044194), so the floor is not guessed. Reported alongside ve_disp_new_over_old = median displacement of the 4 tables at layers the control does NOT carry, divided by the median over the 4 layers it does. REDUNDANCY ENGAGED means ve_disp_new_over_old < 0.5. Companion shape observable ve_xtable_cos_median, the median cosine between corresponding rows of tables at adjacent VE layers, which distinguishes 'the new tables barely moved' from 'the new tables moved to the same place as the old ones'.
competing_explanation: Under-training rather than redundancy. At ~1000 steps each of eight tables receives roughly half the gradient signal per parameter that each of four would; low displacement in the new tables could mean they had no time, not that they had nothing to learn. The two are separable: under-training predicts uniformly depressed displacement across ALL eight tables relative to the control's four, while redundancy predicts a split between the original layers and the new ones.
falsifier: Stride 2->1 lowers val_bpb by more than the measured noise band in a yoked pair while the step count difference stays inside the band, AND the four newly added tables show end-of-run displacement from init comparable to the four the control already had. That is densification paying without redundancy, and this mechanism is dead.
mediator: The marginal NON-redundant content each additional independent value-embedding table carries. All eight tables are indexed by the same token id and read the same 8192-row vocabulary; the only thing that can make the fifth through eighth tables worth their parameters is that they learn something the first four did not. The mediator is the divergence of the newly added tables from the ones already present, not their presence.
name: ve_marginal_table_redundancy

activation_observable: steps completed inside the charged 300s and tokens_per_sec, printed by BOTH arms of the same wave, together with the existing parameter-count block's value_embeds entry (control 4*8192*256 = 8,388,608; treatment 8*8192*256 = 16,777,216) which proves the density actually changed. ENGAGED means the treatment's step count sits below its yoked control's by more than the measured band. Non-activation here is inconclusive about the traffic story, never evidence that the extra tables were free.
competing_explanation: Host CPU contention or a co-tenant moved the step count, not the tables. This is the standing hazard on this box and it is the whole reason the comparison is a same-wave yoked pair on separate GPUs; a step-count gap that reproduces across two independent waves is the tables, one that does not is the host.
falsifier: The stride-1 arm completes the same number of steps in the charged 300s as its yoked stride-2 control, within the band measured from concurrent controls. Then doubling the tables is not priced in traffic at this size, no throughput correction is owed, and any val_bpb difference must be attributed elsewhere.
mediator: Bytes moved per step by the value-embedding gathers and their optimizer state, rather than the FLOPs they add. Doubling the tables doubles a 8192 x 256 bf16 gather per step per doubled layer and doubles the AdamW first/second-moment traffic on that group; the arithmetic added is negligible next to the model's GEMMs. Inside a FIXED 300 charged seconds that traffic converts directly into fewer steps, and fewer steps is a real loss cost, not a nuisance.
name: ve_table_traffic_prices_the_step

activation_observable: ve_emb_rms_final per table against the exactly known init value 0.044194, and ve_disp_ratio = ||VE_final - VE_init||_F / ||VE_init||_F over the concatenated tables. In the frozen arm these must read 0.044194 and 0.0 exactly, which is what proves the freeze applied rather than being asserted; in the trained arm ve_disp_ratio > 0 is what proves content learning engaged at all. Both are single epilogue reductions after the charged clock stops.
competing_explanation: Freezing the tables also removes a parameter group from AdamW and changes the trainable-parameter count and the effective regularization, so a frozen-vs-trained difference could be an optimizer or capacity effect wearing a content label. A cheaper discriminator that does not touch the group structure: keep the tables trainable but re-initialize them from a different seed and check whether val_bpb moves by more than the band - if the specific content mattered, seed-level content variation should register.
falsifier: An arm whose value_embeds are FROZEN at their random init (gates still trained, everything else identical) finishes more than the measured band ABOVE the arm with trained tables. Then the content is doing the work, the pathway alone is not enough, and this mechanism is dead. The comparison must be run at the SAME number of injection layers so density is not confounded with content.
mediator: Whether the value-embedding win is carried by the gated additive side-path into V - an extra input-dependent per-head term added to every value vector - or by the learned CONTENT of the token-indexed table. These are different goods with different prices: the pathway costs a 32-channel gate per layer, the content costs a full vocab-sized table plus its optimizer state.
name: ve_pathway_not_table_content

activation_observable: Three numbers, printed by EVERY arm including the control so each is a comparison and not a bare value, all derived by walking the CONSTRUCTED modules (self.window_sizes) rather than echoing the cfg string: n_long_layers (count of layers whose window >= config.sequence_len; control = 2), n_short_layers (control = 6), and attn_flops_short_M / attn_flops_long_M, the estimate_flops attention term split by layer class (control: long layers carry 25.2 of the 62.9 MFLOP/token attention term, i.e. 40%, against a total of 239.1 MFLOP/token). A run in which attn_flops_long_M is unchanged from the control has not exercised this mechanism whatever happened to val_bpb, and is INCONCLUSIVE about it. Report num_steps beside them, since the throughput leg is what any FLOP change is being traded for.
competing_explanation: STEP COUNT, and nothing else, via the campaign step law. Removing a global layer removes 12.6 MFLOP/token (5.3% of the model) and can only add steps; the cheap explanation of any val_bpb movement is therefore the step law alone, evaluated against the YOKED control of the same wave rather than against any earlier run, because byte-identical control code has ranged 621 to 1021 steps on this contended host. The discriminating observation is (num_steps, step_ms_med, attn_flops_long_M) read together: the mechanism survives only if val_bpb beats its own step-law prediction. A second competing explanation is PLACEMENT rather than COUNT -- 'SSSSSSSL' both halves the global layers and moves the surviving one to the end, and r34_best_global_layer_placement_does_not_transfer_across_models shows the sign of a placement effect did not even survive a change of model inside one family, so a null or a loss here cannot be attributed to count until a count-matched, placement-different arm ('SSSLSSSS' with the forced-long final layer) has been run. Third: r34_final_layer_forced_global_by_construction means one long layer is present by fiat in every arm, so 'one global layer' is the floor this design can reach, not zero.
falsifier: Run 'SSSSSSSL' (one global layer instead of two, short span unchanged at 1024) as a yoked same-wave pair against the byte-identical control. KILLED: the arm loses val_bpb by more than the measured band even though it gains steps -- that would show the second global layer is genuinely load-bearing and that the SSSL ratio is already at or past the minimum, which in turn predicts that any FURTHER thinning of global reach is a losing direction. ALSO KILLED, in the other direction: 'SSLL' (four global layers) beats the control on val_bpb despite costing FLOPs and steps, which would say the stack is starved of global routing and that the campaign has been shrinking the wrong thing. DID NOT ENGAGE: n_long_layers printed by the arm is still 2, meaning window_pattern did not apply -- score nothing, this is the L007 shape where a byte-different file builds an identical model. SURVIVES: the arm is inside the band on val_bpb while n_long_layers is 1, i.e. one of the two global layers was redundant, which makes global-layer COUNT a cheaper lever than short-window size and reorders the queue.
mediator: The NUMBER AND SPACING OF FULL-CONTEXT LAYERS in the stack -- the count of L characters in window_pattern after _compute_window_sizes tiles it and then overwrites window_sizes[-1] with the long window. At depth 8 the baseline 'SSSL' yields S,S,S,L,S,S,S,L: six short layers and two global ones, i.e. one global layer in four, and every query position reaches every earlier position in ONE hop through either of them. This mediator is not the short span and is not the attention FLOP count. It is how many independent full-context routing opportunities the residual stream gets, and where in depth they sit. It is the quantity that decides whether the short span is load-bearing at all: with a global layer present, out-of-window evidence still reaches a position, so shrinking the short window removes redundant reach rather than reach. Changing it is cheap and orthogonal to swdiv -- 'SSSSSSSL' halves the global layers to one, 'SSLSSSLL'-style patterns move them, 'SSLL' doubles them -- and unlike swdiv it changes the attention FLOP FLOOR that no short-window shrink can go below: the two long layers contribute 2 x 12 x n_head x head_dim x 2048 of the estimate_flops attention term, which is 40% of the model's attention FLOPs and is untouched by any value of swdiv.
name: window_pattern_ratio_sets_global_pathways

activation_observable: global_head_frac = (number of attention heads across the whole model whose window >= config.sequence_len) / (n_layer * n_head), computed by walking the constructed per-head window assignment, printed by every arm. Control = 2 long layers * 4 heads / 32 = 0.25 by layer granularity; the head-split arm at 1 global head of 4 in every layer = 0.25 as well, which is the point -- the two arms hold the global FRACTION fixed and vary only its GRANULARITY, so an identical global_head_frac with a different per-layer distribution is exactly what proves the edit applied. Print alongside it n_attn_kernel_calls_per_layer (1 for the control, 2 for the split arm) and flops_per_token_M, so that a step-time change can be attributed to kernel count rather than to arithmetic.
competing_explanation: KERNEL SHAPE, not architecture. Splitting one fa3 call into two halves the head count per call and doubles the launches, and this campaign already has a standing result that the implementation and not the mechanism decides the verdict for attention masking. A B-arm loss is therefore explained more cheaply by launch overhead and smaller GEMMs than by the local/global partition, and is only attributable to the partition if step_ms_med and num_steps are inside the yoked control's band. Second competing explanation: HEAD COUNT. At model_dim 512 and head_dim 128 there are only 4 heads, so 'one global head' is 25% of the layer's attention width and cannot be tuned finely; a null result may mean the granularity available at this width is too coarse to distinguish the two partitions, which is a statement about our aspect ratio and not about the mechanism. Third: r34_local_branch_weight_grows_with_depth_and_training reports the learned local weight rising with depth, so a uniform per-layer head split may be the wrong shape even if head granularity is the right idea.
falsifier: Build a FLOP-matched pair and run them in one wave: (A) the SSSL control at swdiv 4, and (B) every layer with 3 heads at a short span and 1 head at full context, the span chosen so flops_per_token_M matches A to within 1%. KILLED: B loses val_bpb to A by more than the measured band -- global reach at every depth is worth less than local width where SSSL puts it, and the layer-granular partition stands. KILLED THE OTHER WAY (i.e. confirmed): B beats A at equal FLOPs, which would mean the campaign should be tuning head allocation rather than span. DID NOT ENGAGE: global_head_frac printed by B is 0.0 or 1.0, meaning the per-head window never applied -- fa3.flash_attn_func takes ONE window_size for the whole call, so B requires two calls (a local-head call and a global-head call) with the head dimension split and the outputs concatenated before c_proj, and an implementation that silently falls back to a single call is byte-different with an identical model. That failure is not evidence against the mechanism. A THIRD outcome worth naming in advance: B costs step time despite matched FLOPs, because two smaller fa3 calls per layer launch more kernels than one; if step_ms_med rises while flops_per_token_M is flat, the finding is a kernel-shape cost and the mechanism is untested, not refuted.
mediator: WHERE THE LOCAL/GLOBAL BOUNDARY IS DRAWN -- across layers, as SSSL does, or across heads inside every layer, as LS-attention does. The baseline gives each layer a single window applied to all n_head = model_dim / 128 = 4 heads uniformly (Block.forward passes one window_size tuple straight into fa3.flash_attn_func). The alternative allocates, in EVERY layer, some heads to a short span and the rest to full context, so that global reach is available at every depth instead of at two depths. At depth 8 with 4 heads this is a genuinely different partition of the same FLOP budget: 3 local heads of span s plus 1 global head in all 8 layers costs the same attention FLOPs as SSSL with short span (8/6)*(3/4)*s, so the two can be compared at MATCHED attention FLOPs, which is what makes this a mechanism and not a knob. The physical claim is that a model needs global reach at every depth more than it needs a wide local span at any depth, and that the layer-granular SSSL partition is a coarse approximation to a head-granular one.
name: local_global_split_within_a_layer

activation_observable: bpb_eval_sw1024, bpb_eval_sw512, bpb_eval_sw256 and bpb_eval_all2048: four validation-bpb values from the frozen evaluate_bpb on ONE set of trained weights with only the short-layer window varied, printed in the epilogue after the charged clock stops, so they cannot move val_bpb or num_steps. The activation test is that they are not all equal: three identical values prove the mutation did not reach the forward path. Report them next to the run's own val_bpb (which must equal bpb_eval_sw1024 for the control, and is the integrity check on the probe). Emitting this in the CONTROL is what makes it useful -- it prices the swdiv arm before the arm is launched.
competing_explanation: TRAIN/EVAL MISMATCH. A weights-fixed probe narrows the window at evaluation time on a model that was TRAINED at 1024, so any bpb rise conflates 'the information was needed' with 'the model was tuned for a mask it is no longer given' -- exactly the training-inference mismatch that r34_pure_swa_collapse_is_out_of_window_only_and_recoverable shows is large and separable from the structural loss. The rise is therefore an UPPER bound on the true cost of training at 512, and a null is far stronger than a positive. Ruling it out properly requires the reverse probe, which the swdiv arm supplies for free: evaluate the swdiv-4 model at 512 (matched) and at 1024 (widened); if widening a 512-trained model does not lower its bpb, the missing information genuinely was not there. The second competing explanation is EVAL NOISE: evaluate_bpb runs over a fixed EVAL_TOKENS budget on the same val shard with no sampling, so the three values differ only through the mask and share every other source of variance, which is what makes this probe unusually sensitive -- but the band it must be compared against is still the concurrently measured control band, not zero.
falsifier: The probe itself is the experiment and it costs no GPU wave: in the epilogue of the CONTROL, after total_training_time is fixed, call the frozen evaluate_bpb three more times on the same weights with the short-layer window set to 1024 (as trained), 512 and 256, and once more with every layer set to 2048. KILLED: bpb_eval_sw512 exceeds bpb_eval_sw1024 by more than the measured noise band, which says the 512-to-1024 band is carrying real predictive signal and predicts swdiv 2 -> 4 must pay for its steps. STRONGLY CONFIRMED: bpb_eval_sw512 is inside the band of bpb_eval_sw1024 AND bpb_eval_all2048 is also inside it -- the model is not using out-of-window evidence at all at this scale and horizon, in which case the short span is pure cost and the right arm is not swdiv 4 but the smallest span the kernel supports. DID NOT ENGAGE: the three bpb values are bit-identical, which means window_sizes was mutated after the forward path had already captured it (Block.forward receives window_size as an argument from GPT.forward's loop over self.window_sizes, so the mutation must happen on the module attribute before the call, not on a local) -- re-run, score nothing, and do not read identical numbers as a flat curve.
mediator: THE DISTRIBUTION OF PREDICTIVE DEPENDENCY DISTANCE THAT THE TRAINED MODEL ACTUALLY EXPLOITS -- how much of val_bpb is produced by evidence more than 512 tokens back. Every argument for and against swdiv 2 -> 4 reduces to this one unmeasured quantity, and the campaign has never measured it. It is measurable WITHOUT spending a training run: the window is an inference-time mask, so on the FINISHED baseline weights, after the charged clock has stopped, val_bpb can be re-evaluated with self.window_sizes rewritten to any divisor. The mediator is the resulting curve bpb(eval_window). If bpb is flat from 2048 down to 512, the evidence beyond 512 tokens is not being used by this model on this corpus and swdiv 2 -> 4 is close to free in quality; if it rises steeply, the span is load-bearing and the arm is buying steps with real information. Note the asymmetry that makes this cheap and honest: it is a WEIGHTS-FIXED probe, so it measures what the trained-at-1024 model uses, which is an upper bound on what a trained-at-512 model would have needed -- a model trained with the narrower window can relearn to route the same information through the two global layers, so a flat curve is decisive evidence FOR the arm while a steep curve is only suggestive against it.
name: effective_context_actually_used

activation_observable: first8_attn_mass_short and first8_attn_mass_long: the mean attention probability assigned to key positions 0-7, averaged over heads and over query positions at t >= 1024, computed separately for short-window and long-window layers on ONE held-out batch in the epilogue after the charged clock stops (a dense scaled_dot_product_attention recompute with the same causal-plus-window mask; its cost is irrelevant because it is off the charged clock). Print sink_starved_frac = 1 - short_window / sequence_len alongside, derived from the CONSTRUCTED self.window_sizes, so the arm proves its own window changed: control 0.50, swdiv-4 arm 0.75. Emit all three in the control too. A short-layer value that is structurally forced to zero for the queries being averaged (which it is, for t >= W) is the wrong average -- the quantity that matters is the LONG layers' first8 mass, which measures whether a sink exists at all in this model, and the short layers' first8 mass restricted to queries at t < W, which measures whether the model uses it where it can.
competing_explanation: THE SINK MAY NOT EXIST HERE, which is the cheapest explanation and must be tested before anything else -- every source for it (2601.22966 at 2B/120B, 2512.10411 on Qwen3-4B) studies models PRETRAINED WITH FULL ATTENTION, where the sink was learned under a mask that always exposed position 0. Our six short layers never expose position 0 to the second half of any sequence during training, so the model may have built its rescaling elsewhere -- for instance at the left edge of each window, or in the two global layers, or not at all, since baseline/train.py already applies QK-norm which pins the logit scale that the sink is hypothesised to be rescaling. Second competing explanation: any bpb recovery from a first-k exemption could come from the k extra keys as CONTENT (the first tokens of a packed document genuinely predict its continuation) rather than as a sink, and the two are separated by exempting a mid-sequence block of 64 keys instead of the first 64 -- if that helps equally, it is content, not sink. Third: step count, as always; a mask change that alters kernel shape can move num_steps and the step law must be charged against the yoked same-wave control before any bpb difference is attributed to the mask.
falsifier: Two-step, and the second step is only run if the first fires. Step 1, free: in the epilogue of the control and of the swdiv-4 arm, densely recompute attention probabilities for one held-out batch and report first8_attn_mass_short. KILLED IMMEDIATELY if the control's first8_attn_mass_short is already at or below the uniform-attention level (8/E[window]) -- a model trained from scratch with a window never built a sequence-initial sink, there is nothing to starve, and any swdiv loss must be explained by lost evidence instead. Step 2, only if the control shows a real sink AND swdiv 4 loses bpb: run swdiv 4 with the first 64 key positions exempted from the short-layer mask. KILLED if that arm does not recover a detectable share of the lost bpb -- the loss was evidence, not sink access. CONFIRMED if it recovers most of it at essentially unchanged num_steps, which would make 'narrow window plus sink exemption' strictly better than either endpoint. DID NOT ENGAGE for step 2: first8_attn_mass_short in the exempted arm is unchanged from the plain swdiv-4 arm, meaning the exemption never reached the kernel -- fa3.flash_attn_func's window_size argument expresses a contiguous band and CANNOT express a band-plus-prefix mask, so this arm requires either an explicit mask path or a second attention call over the first 64 keys, and a silent fallback to the plain window is the L007 failure shape. Non-activation is inconclusive and must not retire the mechanism.
mediator: THE FRACTION OF QUERY POSITIONS IN THE SHORT LAYERS THAT CANNOT SEE THE SEQUENCE-INITIAL TOKENS. A causal window of width W at sequence length T cuts every query at position t >= W off from position 0, so the starved fraction is 1 - W/T: 0.50 at the baseline's 1024 and 0.75 at swdiv 4's 512, in six of eight layers. This is a distinct failure channel from lost long-range EVIDENCE, because the initial tokens are reported to act as a rescaling/no-op sink rather than as content, and losing them destabilises the attention distribution rather than removing information. It is separable and cheaply repairable: re-admitting a handful of initial key positions restores sink access at a FLOP cost of k/W per short layer, roughly 100/512 of nothing, and the same reference measures its throughput cost as within noise (30.72 vs 30.65 k tok/s). If swdiv 2 -> 4 loses bpb, this mechanism says WHICH loss it is and offers a repair that keeps the FLOP saving.
name: sink_access_under_a_shrinking_window

activation_observable: the trainer must print, per run, momentum_ramp_end_progress = total_training_time_at_the_first_step_where_get_muon_momentum returns 0.95, divided by TIME_BUDGET; plus muon_momentum logged alongside progress at every logged step. Two runs claiming to differ in this mechanism must show momentum_ramp_end_progress values that actually differ; if the field is absent or identical, the comparison is inconclusive, not negative.
competing_explanation: The cheaper explanation is pure step count: halving the batch roughly doubles the number of optimizer updates in 300 seconds, and 2512.13705 reports (r21_batch_above_bopt_gives_identical_step_curves) that loss curves across batch sizes nearly coincide when plotted against STEPS. Under that explanation the momentum ramp is irrelevant and the entire -0.007953 is bought with updates. It must be ruled out by holding tokens-per-step fixed while moving only the ramp length, which is exactly the deconfounding design.
falsifier: A yoked pair at the BASELINE 524288 tokens/step in which the only change is rescaling the ramp length from 300 steps to whatever holds the completed fraction at the half-batch value (about 150 steps, so the ramp ends near 15% of the run) shows a val_bpb difference from its concurrent control that is inside the measured noise band. That would mean the ramp's completion fraction carries none of the batch-halving effect, and the mechanism is dead regardless of how the step-count arm turns out.
mediator: the fraction of the 300-second run that elapses before get_muon_momentum(step) saturates at 0.95 - equivalently the share of the run spent at a SHORTENED momentum averaging horizon. The ramp is indexed by step while lr and weight decay are indexed by progress, so tokens-per-step sets this fraction: at 524288 tokens/step the 300-step ramp ends near 30% of the run, at 262144 near 15%.
name: momentum_ramp_completion_fraction

activation_observable: per-step muon_update_rms = mean over Muon-owned parameter tensors of ||delta_W||_F / sqrt(numel(W)), printed at the logged steps (must cover at least steps 1, 50, 150, 300 and 600). The mechanism has engaged only if this trace changes across the ramp in the unmodified run and is measurably flatter in the RMS-corrected variant; an absent or constant-by-construction trace makes the run inconclusive.
competing_explanation: Gradient-noise averaging: a lower beta early gives a shorter EMA window over noisy minibatch gradients, and the benefit may come from the signal-to-noise ratio of the momentum matrix fed into Newton-Schulz rather than from the size of the resulting step. This is cheaper because it needs no coupling to the learning rate at all, and it predicts the RMS-corrected variant will still move val_bpb.
falsifier: A variant that keeps the 300-step momentum ramp but multiplies the Muon learning rate by sqrt((1+beta_t)/(1-beta_t)) / sqrt((1+0.95)/(1-0.95)) so that update RMS is held at its terminal value throughout the ramp, run yoked against the unmodified control, shows a val_bpb difference inside the measured noise band AND leaves the measured Muon update RMS trace flat. That would show the ramp acts through gradient averaging rather than through update magnitude, killing this mechanism.
mediator: the RMS magnitude of the Muon update. Under Kimi update-RMS matching the Muon update scales as sqrt((1-beta)/(1+beta)), so raising beta from 0.85 to 0.95 shrinks the effective step size at fixed learning rate; the momentum ramp is therefore also a descending learning-rate ramp superimposed on the progress-indexed lr multiplier, and its length in steps decides how many updates are taken at the larger effective step.
name: momentum_ramp_as_implicit_step_size_ramp

activation_observable: steps (final step count), tokens_per_step, and total_training_time must be printed per run, and the treatment and control of a wave must show the step counts the design assumed - a batch change that does not move the step count by the expected factor means the intervention did not engage and the comparison is inconclusive.
competing_explanation: The momentum-ramp completion fraction (mechanism momentum_ramp_completion_fraction) rides along with every batch change under the current step-indexed ramp, so any raw batch-size A/B credits it to update count for free. The cheaper alternative to both is throughput: a smaller batch may simply change loader and kernel efficiency, changing step count for reasons that have nothing to do with optimisation - which is why steps must be read from the run and never assumed to scale exactly as 1/tokens_per_step.
falsifier: The deconfounding run at fixed 524288 tokens/step with only the momentum-ramp length rescaled reproduces a majority of the -0.007953 batch-halving effect (i.e. its yoked delta is more negative than about -0.004 and outside the measured band). That would show schedule indexing, not update count, is doing the work at our batch size, and this mechanism is refuted.
mediator: the number of optimizer updates completed inside the 300-second budget. Tokens-per-step converts wall-clock into updates; every schedule-shape term is second order at a large batch because gradient noise is already low.
name: update_count_dominates_at_our_batch

activation_observable: ema_updates, the count of EMA updates actually applied, printed by the treatment; together with the derived retention decay**ema_updates, which is the fraction of the evaluated average that is still its own initial value. A value near 1 means the average never moved and the run evaluated the weights as they stood at ema_start, whatever the loss says. The control does not emit ema_updates at all, so the diagnostic separates the arms by construction; the informative reading is not whether it is above zero but whether decay**ema_updates is small.
competing_explanation: THE AVERAGE IS EVALUATED AT A DIFFERENT POINT IN TRAINING, not merely at a smoother one. ema_start=0.6 begins accumulating at 60 percent of the run, so a slow decay biases the evaluated weights toward that earlier point and any loss difference is confounded with simply having trained less. This is not hypothetical: R9EMA_P1_s0_treat read +0.051008 against its yoked control with 0.999**199 = 0.8195 of the average still its initialisation. Discriminating observations: report decay**ema_updates alongside val_bpb, and require it below 0.05 before reading the delta as an averaging effect at all; and compare treatments at matched ema_start so the window is the only thing varying.
falsifier: ENGAGED-AND-WRONG (kills the mechanism): an arm whose decay**ema_updates is below 0.05, so the average is genuinely over the tail, still fails to beat its yoked control by the counterbalanced resolution. That would mean the final-step weights are not meaningfully noisier than a tail centroid at this budget, and the whole premise -- that evaluation inherits last-step noise worth averaging away -- is wrong here. DID-NOT-ENGAGE: ema_updates reads 0, or val_bpb matches the control to six decimals; re-run, score nothing. NOTE the asymmetry: a LOSS at high retention says nothing about the mechanism and everything about the parameterisation, which is why retention must be reported before the delta is interpreted.
mediator: WHICH POINT ON THE WEIGHT TRAJECTORY IS EVALUATED. The benchmark scores the parameters as they stand at the final optimizer step, so val_bpb inherits whatever gradient noise that one step happened to carry. An exponential moving average over the tail replaces that single point with a weighted centroid of the last 1/(1-decay) updates, which is a different point in parameter space, not a different training run. The quantity that decides whether the swap helps is therefore the AVERAGING WINDOW measured in updates, 1/(1-decay), relative to the number of updates the budget actually delivers. At a 300-second budget this benchmark produces a few hundred optimizer steps, so a decay tuned at a run of tens of thousands of steps averages over a window longer than the run itself and the average never leaves its own initialisation.
name: tail_weight_average_decouples_eval_from_the_last_step
notes: Registered after R9EMA measured a large valid negative under a decay that made the average meaningless (L092). The campaign had been testing weight averaging with no mechanism record behind it, so there was no mediator to state and nothing that forced the window-versus-budget question to be asked before a wave was spent.
